title: Take one terminal block off a DIN rail with a screwdriver without disturbing its neighbours
instruction: Take the blue terminal block off the DIN rail with the screwdriver and put it in the tray, and leave the two beige blocks where they are.
context: Rewiring a control panel means taking single blocks off a terminal strip. A latched block is released with a flat screwdriver in the slot at its foot, then tipped off its fixed hook, without loosening its neighbours.
setup: On the table in front of the arms: a steel TS35 x 7.5 top-hat DIN rail, 500 mm long, with a zinc end bracket 4.2 cm in from each end, screwed flat to the table, open side up and running left to right, its centre 0.30 m in front of the arm bases and 0.04 m right of their midline. Latched on it, 33 mm apart centre to centre: three polyamide push-in terminal blocks (5.1 mm thick along the rail, 65 mm long across it, 36 mm tall, 7.6 g), beige, blue, beige from the left, the blue one 2 cm right of the rail's centre. Each has a rigid fixed hook under the far lip (2.5 mm reach) and a sprung foot under the near lip (2.0 mm reach, 1.0 N/mm, up to 3.5 mm out), opened through a release slot at the near end (2.4 mm across x 4.8 mm along the rail, 9 mm deep, open at the top, between the housing and a 3.0 mm tab on the foot). A flat-blade screwdriver (blade 3.5 x 1.0 mm, 75 mm overall, 60 g) stands handle up in a black plastic holder (40 x 40 x 50 mm), 0.20 m in front of the arm bases and 0.08 m left of their midline. An empty, open black plastic tray (inside 170 x 64 mm, walls 3 mm thick and 12 mm high), its centre 0.18 m in front of the arm bases and 0.22 m right of their midline.
scoring: At the end of the run: 1.0 if the blue block is released (the gripper open and not touching it) and resting still on the tray's floor (its lowest point within 2 mm of the floor) for 1 s, with both beige blocks undisturbed (still latched and within 1 mm of where they started along the rail); 0.75 in the tray (centre inside its inner walls, lowest point below their tops), released or still held; 0.5 off the rail (base 20 mm or more above the lips, or centre outside the rail's footprint); 0.25 its sprung foot released (its tooth 2.0 mm or more out past its latched position, measured against the rail, or the near end lifted 6.5 mm or more off the lip); else 0 (a shifted or tipped block still latched scores 0). Capped at 0.25 if a beige block was disturbed.
reset_notes: Put the blue block back between the beige blocks: hook its far end under the far lip, then press its near end down until the sprung foot clicks. Stand the screwdriver back in its holder, handle up. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz (-E device=cpu). Generic push-in terminal block of this task's own design, specified as a buildable equivalent: rigid fixed hook; sprung foot as a 1 N/mm slider (release 2.0 N at the lip's edge) opened through a 2.4 mm release slot. Collision simplified to boxes and convex pieces. Blade 1.0 mm thick (0.7 mm tunnelled in PhysX). Rail lips 2 mm (1 mm real). Release read from the robot's contact force on the block.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the blue block stayed latched); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 933); held in the tray: 0.75; lifted off the rail and held: 0.5; foot levered out and held: 0.25; same motions without the screwdriver: 0.0
